text:
Marathon Petroleum stock rose 0.24% today on minimal daily movement, but the two-week 13.2% surge reflects the rollercoaster in crude oil prices and geopolitical risk. Oil prices have swung wildly — spiking to $110+ when Iran escalated Strait of Hormuz attacks last week, then sliding this week after Trump announced sanctions relief on Russian crude, which raised hopes of increased global supply. Refineries running at 93.5% utilization mean MPC benefits when oil volatility creates refining spreads (the profit margin between crude costs and finished fuel sales), and the recent churn has kept that spread attractive.

The oil market is now caught between competing forces: supply fears from Middle East tension versus relief from potential Russian crude returning to markets. For a refiner like MPC, this uncertainty swings both ways — tighter supplies mean higher crude costs that can pinch margins, but the current elevated prices and high refinery utilization rates remain profitable. The near-term direction hinges on whether sanctions relief actually materializes and how much Russian supply actually reaches markets.
